name: Cable Lateral Raise
summary: An isolation exercise that targets the lateral deltoid using a cable machine for continuous tension throughout shoulder abduction.

setup: Set the cable pulley to waist or hip height and attach a single D-handle.
Stand sideways to the cable tower with your feet hip-width apart.
Reach across your body with the far arm and grip the handle with your palm facing down or inward.
Step away from the machine until tension is placed on the cable, keeping an upright posture and a soft bend in the working elbow.
steps: Raise your arm out to the side in a wide arc, leading slightly with the elbow until your upper arm reaches shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top to emphasize peak contraction on the lateral deltoid.
Lower the cable smoothly under control along the same path back across your torso to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise your arm outward, and inhale as you lower the weight back to your side.
cues: Reach outward toward the wall rather than lifting upward.
Lead with the elbow, not the wrist.
Keep your shoulders depressed and traps relaxed.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso or using momentum to jerk the cable upward.
common_faults.correction: Brace the core, maintain an upright stance, and reduce the weight to isolate the shoulder.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the neck and engaging excessive upper trapezius.
common_faults.correction: Keep the shoulder blade down and avoid raising the arm higher than shoulder level.

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbow dynamically like a curl or press.
common_faults.correction: Lock a slight bend in the elbow and maintain that exact angle throughout the entire movement.

precautions: Avoid lifting past parallel if you experience pinching or discomfort in the subacromial space.
